title: Mean Reversion
teaches: Mean reversion as we trade it: a swing trade against a short, unusually fast drop in a leader, bought on the turn and never on the falling price, with the stop a few cents under the flush low, a third off at 3R and 5R and the rest on the trail, and a loss at the stop is the plan working.

facts.quote: In the meanwhile after 3 to 4 days of negative action a bounce is likely outcome.

walkthroughs.title: EQT, August 2011: a leader flush in a fear spike
steps: EQT, August 2011. A leader up 32% falls five straight days, 25.2% in all, in a market sell-off.
Flush day: a 2.2 ATR drop on 2.0x volume, closing on the rising 200-day. A level to lean on. We wait.
2011-08-09: it climbs back over the flush close. Buy at market, 26.76. Stop a few cents under the low, 26.00.
Failure mode: a second flush under the low. Instead it closes near its high; 3R prints next day. Trim a third.

walkthroughs.title: KRYS, August 2023: an earnings flush with a level
steps: KRYS, August 2023. A leader up 59% slides four days, 17.9%. The report on 2023-08-07 is the flush day.
It is 12.6% under a rising 50-day, still 20% above its 200-day. A 3.3 ATR drop on 4.0x volume. We wait.
2023-08-08: it opens above the flush close. Buy at market, 109.13. Stop a few cents under the lows, 106.88.
Failure mode: a weak close. Instead it closes at 3R and 5R prints two sessions later. Trim a third at each.

walkthroughs.title: ACMR, September 2020: the post-blow-off snapback
steps: ACMR, September 2020. A stock up 79% runs parabolic, then breaks. Three down days, 38.6% lost, 39% under its 10-session high.
The flush: 3.5 ATR on 3.5x volume, the heaviest of the chart. RSI(2) at 0. Five stretch marks. We wait.
2020-09-09: it turns. Buy at market, 20.00. Stop a few cents under the lows, 19.29, which is 3.5% wide.
Failure mode: a stall. Instead it bounces to the 20-day, 8.1R at best, then drifts sideways.

questions.q: In one line, what is a mean-reversion long?
choices: A bounce trade after a fast, deep drop
A breakout from a quiet, flat base
A hold for months in a rising leader
A bet that a slow decline keeps going
questions.answer: A bounce trade after a fast, deep drop
questions.why: A bounce trade after a fast, deep drop. It is a swing trade against an unusually fast move, aimed at a return to a short average. Stockbee: extremes tend to mean revert in short time frames.
questions.lesson_line: We trade the snapback after a fast drop, not the drift.

wrong.A breakout from a quiet, flat base: That is a base breakout. Mean reversion buys after a drop, not after quiet.
wrong.A hold for months in a rising leader: That is a trend hold. A snapback trade is short.
wrong.A bet that a slow decline keeps going: A slow, controlled decline is a skip for this setup. We want a fast, deep drop.

questions.q: We buy a leader flush only when the stock sat above its 50-day and 200-day before the drop.
questions.why: True. The card wants a leader above its 200-day and 50-day the day before the flush. Connors: look for buying opportunities when above the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Buy the dip in strength. A stock under its 200-day is not our dip.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: Stretch mark 3 is the 2-period RSI under ___.
questions.why: 5. Connors found returns were higher buying an RSI dip below 5 than one below 10.
questions.lesson_line: RSI(2) under 5 is the deep dip. Under 10 is only a dip.

questions.q: On a flush, we buy the turn, not the falling price.
questions.why: True. We wait for the first sign the sellers are done. StockCharts: the RSI(2) signal can be early, because moves often continue after it.
questions.lesson_line: A falling price is not a trigger. The turn is.

questions.q: Where does the stop go on a mean-reversion long?
choices: A few cents under the flush low
At the 20-day average
A fixed 5% under your fill
Under the flush day's high
questions.answer: A few cents under the flush low
questions.why: A few cents under the flush low, or the turn day's low if that is lower. Kell puts the stop just below the low of the reversal bar.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the flush low.

wrong.At the 20-day average: The 20-day is where the bounce may run, not where the trade is wrong.
wrong.A fixed 5% under your fill: A fixed percent ignores where the sellers gave up. The stop sits under the low.
wrong.Under the flush day's high: The high is above your entry, so a stop there would end the trade at once. The stop sits under the low.

questions.q: Because the bounce is short, we can skip the stop on a mean-reversion trade.
questions.why: False. Every position has a real stop order with the broker. Connors does not advocate stops; that is not ours.
questions.lesson_line: Short trade, real stop. The stop is the exit.

questions.q: Which of these ticks stretch mark 2?
choices: A close under the lower Bollinger band
An intraday tag of the lower band
A close above the upper band
A close under the 50-day
questions.answer: A close under the lower Bollinger band
questions.why: A close under the lower Bollinger band. A tag of the lower band is not a signal on its own. Bollinger: tags are just tags.
questions.lesson_line: Mark 2 is a close under the lower band, not a touch.

wrong.An intraday tag of the lower band: Bollinger: tags of the bands are just tags, not signals.
wrong.A close above the upper band: That is a stretch up, not down. Mark 2 is a close under the lower band.
wrong.A close under the 50-day: That is not one of the five marks.

questions.q: A slow, controlled decline with no range or volume expansion is stretched enough to buy.
questions.why: False. A slow, controlled decline is a skip. We want a fast, hard move with range and volume.
questions.lesson_line: Slow and orderly is a pullback. A flush is fast.

questions.q: Which landing spot gives a buyer something to lean on?
choices: The rising 50-day average
The middle of a trading range
Thin air, far from any level
A fresh low with no support near
questions.why: The rising 50-day average. A flush needs a level a buyer can lean on: a prior breakout, a round number, a rising average. Raschke: the worst timing is to buy mid-range.
questions.lesson_line: Flush into a level, not into open space.

wrong.The middle of a trading range: Raschke: the worst thing you can do is to buy in the middle of a trading range.
wrong.Thin air, far from any level: With no level near, nothing stops the fall.
wrong.A fresh low with no support near: No support near means no level to lean on. The flush needs one.

questions.q: Do we buy the turn?
choices: No, no longs under the 200-day
Yes, a 9% drop is big enough
Yes, with a tighter stop
questions.why: No. We take no longs below the 200-day, unless it is a parabolic long. This is a two-day drop with no burst.
questions.lesson_line: Under the 200-day, a bounce is not our trade.

wrong.Yes, a 9% drop is big enough: Size of the drop does not lift the 200-day rule.
wrong.Yes, with a tighter stop: A tighter stop does not change the rule. It only raises the odds of a shakeout.

questions.story: A stock closed 4% under its 200-day after a two-day, 9% drop. There were no gaps and no burst. It turns up at the open.

questions.q: A $7 stock that trades $4 million a day can qualify for a mean-reversion long.
questions.why: False. We trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day. This one fails both halves.
questions.lesson_line: Price and dollar volume come before the chart.

questions.q: The turn prints and you are in. Which order do you use?
choices: A market order
A limit 2% under the print
A stop order above the high
Wait for the close
questions.why: A market order. Entries are market orders, in regular hours. Raschke: I use market orders most of the time.
questions.lesson_line: Entries are market orders in regular hours.

wrong.A limit 2% under the print: A limit under the market can miss the turn. We use market orders.
wrong.A stop order above the high: That waits for a break we do not need. The turn is the trigger.
wrong.Wait for the close: The close of the flush is a B-minus entry. We buy the turn, in regular hours.

questions.q: Prior close 60.00, ATR(14) 1.80, day's low 55.90. How many ATR is the drop?
questions.why: 2.28 ATR. The prior close minus the low, divided by ATR(14). Mark 1 asks for 2 ATR or more, so it is ticked.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the drop in ATRs, not dollars.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the five stretch marks?
choices: A close above the 50-day
RSI(2) under 5
A 2 ATR drop from the prior close
3 or more straight down closes
questions.why: A close above the 50-day. The marks are a 2 ATR drop, a close under the lower band, RSI(2) under 5, 3 or more straight down closes, and a 40% drawdown after a blow-off.
questions.lesson_line: Five marks measure the stretch. Trend is a separate check.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The first trim is a ___ of the position at 3R.
questions.why: third. The hard rule for the first trim is a third at 3R. Another third comes off at 5R and the rest trails.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, then trail the rest.

questions.q: Mean-reversion longs work better in a bear market, even above the 200-day.
questions.why: False. They do worse in bear markets, even above the 200-day. A steady bear market grades B-minus.
questions.lesson_line: A bear market bends the snapback. Be pickier.

questions.q: Where does the stop go?
choices: A few cents under 52.40
A few cents under 52.90
At the 20-day, 54.00
questions.why: A few cents under 52.40, the lower of the two lows. The turn day's low only counts when it is lower.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sits under the lower of the flush low and the turn day's low.

wrong.A few cents under 52.90: That is the higher of the two lows. The stop uses the lower.
wrong.At the 20-day, 54.00: That is above both lows and above the flush area. It is a target area, not a stop.

questions.story: The flush day's low was 52.40. The turn day's low is 52.90. You buy the turn at market.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Take the loss; the stop is the exit
Add half; it is cheaper now
Wait for a close under the low
questions.answer: Take the loss; the stop is the exit
questions.why: Take the loss. The stop is the exit and it only moves up. The full size goes in at one price with one stop.
questions.lesson_line: The stop is the exit. Do not argue with it.

wrong.Add half; it is cheaper now: No adding: the full size goes in at one price with one stop.
wrong.Wait for a close under the low: The stop is a real order. It is not a closing-price suggestion.

questions.story: You bought the turn. Price trades under the flush low, where your stop sits.

questions.q: The setup works best when the VIX is racing toward 30 and short-term breadth is oversold.
questions.why: True. A fast move in the VIX toward 30, oversold breadth and an index also stretched down make the best backdrop. A calm index grades B-minus.
questions.lesson_line: Fear in the market feeds the snapback.

questions.q: The bounce looks strong, so buying 6% above the trigger is fine.
questions.why: False. Never buy more than 4% above the buy point. Chasing costs size: the stop stays put, the distance grows, the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: Miss the chase, keep the size.

questions.q: Do we buy the turn?
choices: No, a report is inside 3 days
Yes, the flush is the edge
Yes, at half size
questions.answer: No, a report is inside 3 days
questions.why: No. We take no new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report. Hold through one only if the trade is up 5R.
questions.lesson_line: A report inside 3 days turns a setup into a coin flip.

wrong.Yes, the flush is the edge: The flush is a setup. A report inside 3 days is a no-buy.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not fix a gap risk. No new buys in the 3 days before a report.

questions.story: A leader flushes for three days and then turns up at the open. Its report is due in two sessions. The chart looks perfect.

questions.q: The 63-day low was 32.00. The close before the slide was 41.60. What was the run?
questions.why: 30%. From the 63-day low to the close before the slide. Form A asks for at least 25%, so this leader qualifies.
questions.lesson_line: A leader flush needs a leader's run first.

questions.q: The highest close of the last 10 sessions was 33.00. Today closes at 19.50. How far down is that?
questions.why: 40.9%. The high minus the close, divided by the high. Mark 5 asks for 40% or more in 10 sessions after a blow-off, so it is ticked.
questions.lesson_line: Mark 5 is a collapse after a blow-off, measured from the 10-session high.

questions.q: You buy at 109.13. The lower of the two lows is 106.93 and the stop sits 5 cents under it. How wide is the stop in percent?
questions.why: 2.06%. The entry minus the stop, divided by the entry. That is inside the 3% the stop usually keeps. KRYS was bought here after its report flush.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the stop in percent before you size.

questions.q: You buy at 26.76 with the stop at 26.00. What price is 3R?
questions.why: 29.04. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of them to the fill. A third comes off there.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: Account 50,000. You risk 0.5% on the trade. Buy at 26.76, stop at 26.00. How many shares?
questions.why: 328 shares. Stop first, then the size from the stop: the dollar risk divided by the fill minus the stop, rounded down.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sets the size. The size never sets the stop.

questions.q: Bought at 40.00, stop at 38.50. A gap-down day makes a first 30-minute low of 37.20. How many R is the loss?
questions.why: 1.87R. The loss at the first 30-minute low, in units of your risk. That is inside the 2R ceiling, so that low becomes the new stop.
questions.lesson_line: On a gap, the first 30 minutes decide. Past 2R, get out.

questions.q: Do you buy the close?
choices: No, wait for the turn
Yes, it is as stretched as it gets
Yes, but at half size
questions.why: No, wait for the turn. Buying the close of the flush is a B-minus: no turn yet. StockCharts: the signal can be early.
questions.lesson_line: A stretch is the setup. The turn is the trigger.

wrong.Yes, it is as stretched as it gets: A stretch is the setup, not the trigger. Moves often continue after the signal.
wrong.Yes, but at half size: Half size is still buying the falling price.

questions.story: A leader's flush day closes on its low, under the lower band, with RSI(2) at 2. Tomorrow could go either way.

questions.q: Is stretch mark 2 ticked?
choices: No, a tag is not a close under
Yes, any touch counts
Yes, it is the strongest mark
questions.answer: No, a tag is not a close under
questions.why: No. Mark 2 needs a close under the lower band. Bollinger: tags of the bands are just tags, not signals.
questions.lesson_line: A tag is a touch. A close under is the mark.

wrong.Yes, any touch counts: A tag of the band is not a signal on its own.
wrong.Yes, it is the strongest mark: The five marks are not ranked. And a tag is not one.

questions.story: A leader slides three days. This morning it tagged the lower Bollinger band, then closed back inside it.

questions.q: Is this a flush to buy?
choices: No, only the second down day
Yes, it broke the 50-day
Yes, gaps always bounce
questions.answer: No, only the second down day
questions.why: No. The first or second down day is a skip. We want a real stretch, and a third straight down close ticks mark 4.
questions.lesson_line: Two red days is a dip. Wait for the stretch.

wrong.Yes, it broke the 50-day: A first break of a level is not a stretch. The setup needs more.
wrong.Yes, gaps always bounce: Nothing always bounces. This is only the second down day.

questions.story: A leader gaps down 3% on its second straight down day. Volume is average and it sits just under its 50-day.

questions.q: Take the turn or pass?
choices: Pass, there is no level to lean on
Take it, 8% in four sessions is plenty
Take it with a wider stop
questions.answer: Pass, there is no level to lean on
questions.why: Pass. The flush needs a level a buyer can lean on, not the middle of a range. Raschke: buying mid-range is the worst timing.
questions.lesson_line: No level, no trade.

wrong.Take it, 8% in four sessions is plenty: A big drop with no level is just a drop. Mid-range grades B-minus.
wrong.Take it with a wider stop: A wider stop only makes the loss bigger. The stop only moves up, never wider.

questions.story: A leader loses 8% in four sessions and stops in the middle of a two-month range. No level is near.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Skip it; it is past 4% above the trigger
Buy at market and widen the stop
Place a limit at 50.00 and wait
questions.answer: Skip it; it is past 4% above the trigger
questions.why: Skip it. Never buy more than 4% above the trigger. Chasing costs size, not risk.
questions.lesson_line: A missed turn is a missed trade, not a new entry.

wrong.Buy at market and widen the stop: The stop only moves up, never wider. And you would be chasing.
wrong.Place a limit at 50.00 and wait: Our entries are market orders on the trigger. A limit under the market is hope, not a trigger.

questions.story: The turn printed at 50.00 while you were in a meeting. You see 52.40 now.

questions.q: What do you do at the open?
choices: Take the 3R trim at the open
Wait for 5R before selling
Move the stop up and hold it all
questions.answer: Take the 3R trim at the open
questions.why: Take the third at the open. A trim level the day opens past is taken at the open.
questions.lesson_line: Opens past a trim level, trim at the open.

wrong.Wait for 5R before selling: The 3R level is past. If a stock opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open.
wrong.Move the stop up and hold it all: The first third comes off at 3R. The stop can move to breakeven after that.

questions.story: You bought at 40.00 with the stop at 38.50. So 3R is 44.50. Next morning the stock opens at 45.10.

questions.q: When does the last third go?
choices: On a close under the 10-day
On the first red day
At the next round number
questions.why: On a close under the 10-day for a fast mover, or the 21-day for a steadier one. A third came off at 3R and another at 5R.
questions.lesson_line: Trail the last third. Sell on a close below the line.

wrong.On the first red day: One red day is noise in a trend. The trail is a close below the line.
wrong.At the next round number: A round number is a level to watch, not the rule. The rule is the trail.

questions.story: You took thirds at 3R and 5R. The snapback has become a fast trend riding its 10-day.

questions.q: What can the stop do now?
choices: Move up to breakeven
Move down to give it room
Widen it to the 20-day
questions.why: Move up to breakeven. The stop goes to breakeven between 2R and 5R, ideally. It only moves up.
questions.lesson_line: After the first trim the stop may go to breakeven. Never down.

wrong.Move down to give it room: The stop only moves up, never down or wider.
wrong.Widen it to the 20-day: That is wider. The stop only moves up.

questions.story: You took the first third at 3R. The rest still has the original stop under the flush low.

questions.q: The honest stop is 3.7% away. Pulling it tighter to keep your usual size is fine.
questions.why: False. Stop first, then the size from the stop. If the honest stop does not fit the risk, skip. The stop only moves up, never wider.
questions.lesson_line: Never squeeze the stop to fit the size.

questions.q: Add to the position?
choices: No, one price, one stop, no adding
Yes, add half at 40.50
Yes, add and move both stops
questions.answer: No, one price, one stop, no adding
questions.why: No. The full size goes in at one price with one stop. A re-entry after a stop-out is a new trade on a new trigger.
questions.lesson_line: One entry, one stop. No adding.

wrong.Yes, add half at 40.50: The full size goes in at one price with one stop; no adding.
wrong.Yes, add and move both stops: No adding, and the stop only moves up.

questions.story: You are in at 40.00 with the stop at 38.50. It bounces 1R, dips back to 40.50 and looks ready again.

questions.q: Take the fourth try?
choices: No, 3 tries a week is the limit
Yes, each turn is a new trade
Yes, at half size
questions.answer: No, 3 tries a week is the limit
questions.why: No. At most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month on one stock. Each try after a stop-out is also a new trade on a new trigger.
questions.lesson_line: Whipsaw is a signal to stop, not to try again.

wrong.Yes, each turn is a new trade: Each turn is a new trade, but the cap is 3 tries in a week.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not lift the cap.

questions.story: You were stopped out on the same name three times this week. A fourth turn prints on Friday.

questions.q: A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold.
questions.why: True. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money.
questions.lesson_line: Dead money gets freed.

questions.q: Which exit plan is NOT ours?
choices: No stop; sell at the 5-day average
A real stop; a third off at 3R
A real stop; trail the last third
questions.answer: No stop; sell at the 5-day average
questions.why: No stop, sell at the 5-day average. Connors does not advocate stops and exits on a move above the 5-day SMA. We keep a real stop and trim in thirds.
questions.lesson_line: We keep a stop and trim in thirds. Connors does not.

wrong.A real stop; a third off at 3R: That is ours: a real stop and a third at 3R.
wrong.A real stop; trail the last third: That is ours: a real stop and a trail on the last third.

questions.q: Where does Kell put his first profit target after a flush?
choices: A retest of the 20 EMA
The 200-day average
The prior all-time high
questions.why: A retest of the 20 EMA. That is Kell's rule. Our house default is a third at 3R, then a third at 5R and the trail.
questions.lesson_line: Know the other rules, then trade ours.

wrong.The 200-day average: Kell names the retest of the 20 EMA, not the 200-day.
wrong.The prior all-time high: Kell names the retest of the 20 EMA.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: Stretch mark 4 is ___ or more straight down closes.
questions.why: 3. Three or more straight down closes tick mark 4. Stockbee: after 3 to 4 days of negative action a bounce is likely.
questions.lesson_line: Count the down closes. Three or more ticks mark 4.

questions.q: Day one's bounce stalls and closes weak. What is that?
choices: The early warning of a failing bounce
A normal shakeout to add on
Proof the flush is complete
questions.answer: The early warning of a failing bounce
questions.why: The early warning. A bounce that stalls and closes weak on day one or two is how the card flags a failing bounce.
questions.lesson_line: A weak close on day one is the early warning.

wrong.A normal shakeout to add on: No adding. A weak close is a warning, not an invitation.
wrong.Proof the flush is complete: A bounce that stalls proves nothing is finished.

questions.q: How does Kullamagi enter his long bounce?
choices: Opening range high, first green candle
The close of the flush day
A limit at the low of the day
questions.answer: Opening range high, first green candle
questions.why: The opening range high or the first green 5-minute candle. He waits for the bounce to start, as we wait for the turn.
questions.lesson_line: Wait for the bounce to start, then buy.

wrong.The close of the flush day: That buys the falling price. Kullamagi waits for the bounce to start.
wrong.A limit at the low of the day: That tries to catch the exact low. He waits for an upward break instead.

questions.q: With an average daily volume of 800,000 shares, owning 12,000 is too many.
questions.why: True. Never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume. 12,000 shares is over 1% of 800,000.
questions.lesson_line: Size by the stop, then check you can get out.

questions.q: Mean-reversion flush or something else?
choices: A moving-average pullback
A mean-reversion flush
An oops reversal
questions.why: A moving-average pullback. It drifts on light volume to a rising line with no big day. A flush is a hard 2 ATR day through the short averages.
questions.lesson_line: A drift is a pullback. A flush is a shock.

wrong.A mean-reversion flush: A flush is a hard, fast day. This is a slow drift with no big day.
wrong.An oops reversal: An oops gaps under the prior day's low and reclaims the prior close the same day. Nothing like that happened here.

questions.story: A leader drifts for six sessions on light volume to its rising 20 EMA. No day drops more than 1 ATR.

questions.q: Which card is this?
choices: Parabolic long
Mean-reversion flush
Moving-average pullback
questions.why: Parabolic long. A multi-day burst of gap downs is the parabolic family. A one-day leader flush with no burst is this card.
questions.lesson_line: A burst of gaps is parabolic. A one-day flush is mean reversion.

wrong.Mean-reversion flush: The flush on this card is a one-day leader flush with no multi-day burst.
wrong.Moving-average pullback: A pullback drifts on light volume. Four gaps and a 45% fall is no drift.

questions.story: A stock gaps down four days in a row and ends 45% off its peak, with a gap down on the last day.

questions.q: Which setup is this?
choices: An undercut and rally
A mean-reversion flush
A parabolic long
questions.why: An undercut and rally. It undercuts a visible level after an ordinary dip and needs no volume. A flush is a hard, fast drop.
questions.lesson_line: An undercut of a level after an ordinary dip is its own setup.

wrong.A mean-reversion flush: A flush is a hard, fast drop. A 3% dip on ordinary volume is not one.
wrong.A parabolic long: A parabolic long is a multi-day burst of gap downs. This is one ordinary dip.

questions.story: A leader dips 3% under a clear support level on ordinary volume, then closes back above it the same day.

questions.q: Flush or something else?
choices: An oops reversal
A mean-reversion flush
A moving-average pullback
questions.why: An oops reversal. It gaps under the prior day's low in an orderly pullback and reclaims the prior close the same day.
questions.lesson_line: Orderly pullback, gap under, reclaim the same day: oops.

wrong.A mean-reversion flush: A flush is a hard, fast drop, not a calm pullback.
wrong.A moving-average pullback: A pullback drifts to a line. It does not gap under and reclaim the prior close.

questions.story: A leader is 6% off its high after a calm pullback. It gaps under the prior day's low, then reclaims the prior close the same day.

questions.q: Why do we pass?
choices: No leader's run behind it
It is above the 200-day
A 2.1 ATR flush is too big
questions.why: No leader's run behind it. Form A wants at least 25% from the 63-day low, and this had 15%. It is a stock rolling over from a top.
questions.lesson_line: No leader's run, no leader flush.

wrong.It is above the 200-day: Being above the 200-day is what the setup wants.
wrong.A 2.1 ATR flush is too big: A 2.1 ATR flush is what a flush looks like. The run before it is what is missing.

questions.story: A stock is up 15% from its 63-day low. It slides four days, a 2.1 ATR flush, and still sits above both averages.

questions.q: Stopped out next day. What did the chart say before you bought?
choices: A broken leader after a parabolic top
A clean leader at support
A slow grind on no volume
questions.answer: A broken leader after a parabolic top
questions.why: A broken leader after a parabolic top. An eight-day slide through the 50-day is a broken leader, not a stretched one.
questions.lesson_line: Eight red days through the 50-day is a break, not a stretch.

wrong.A clean leader at support: Eight down closes through the 50-day is not a clean leader resting at support.
wrong.A slow grind on no volume: The flush came on 3x volume. This was no slow grind.

questions.story: A stock just made a parabolic top, up 58%. It falls eight straight days, 21% in all, through its 50-day. A 3x volume flush comes next and RSI(2) is 0.

questions.q: What now?
choices: Take the loss; rebuy on a new trigger
Buy back at once, it is cheaper
Widen the next stop to give it room
questions.answer: Take the loss; rebuy on a new trigger
questions.why: Take the loss. A second flush on heavier volume means the selling was not done. A re-entry needs a new trigger, as a new trade with its own stop.
questions.lesson_line: A planned loss. Buy again only on a new trigger.

wrong.Buy back at once, it is cheaper: After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again. No trigger, no trade.
wrong.Widen the next stop to give it room: The stop is under the low, where the rule puts it. A wider stop only makes the loss bigger.

questions.story: You buy at 320.55 with the stop at 311.69 after a five-day slide. Two sessions later the market breaks. The stock makes a new low on heavier volume and stops you out.

questions.q: The stop fills. Was the trade a mistake?
choices: No, a planned loss at the stop
Yes, you should have held it
Yes, the stop was too tight
questions.answer: No, a planned loss at the stop
questions.why: No. The stop did its job. A bounce that closes weak on day one is the early warning, and the loss was the plan.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out under the rules is a planned loss, not a mistake.

wrong.Yes, you should have held it: The stop is the exit. It only moves up, never down or wider.
wrong.Yes, the stop was too tight: The stop sat under the lows, where the rules put it. A wider stop only makes the loss bigger.

questions.story: You buy at 105.48 with the stop at 103.39. Day one trades down to 99.80 and closes at 101.13, near its low. The index makes a new low.

questions.q: Take the turn?
choices: Pass; no level to lean on
Take it; 6x volume is a climax
Take it at half size
questions.answer: Pass; no level to lean on
questions.why: Pass. A report-driven drop with no level to lean on keeps falling. Size cannot give it a level.
questions.lesson_line: A report drop with no level keeps falling.

wrong.Take it; 6x volume is a climax: Volume is not a level. Without a level to lean on the drop keeps falling.
wrong.Take it at half size: Size cannot give it a level to lean on.

questions.story: A leader up 27% drops 17.5% in three days after its report, a 3.2 ATR flush on 6x volume. The honest stop is 6.4% away. Nothing sits under it.

questions.q: Which flush grades higher?
choices: B, by a long way
A, it is calmer
They grade the same
questions.why: B. A 4th down day, a level to lean on and fear in the market are the A+ cues. A 2nd day, mid-range, in a calm index is B-minus.
questions.lesson_line: More stretch, a level and fear grade higher.

wrong.A, it is calmer: Calm is a B-minus cue. Fear in the market is the A+ cue.
wrong.They grade the same: The 4th day, the level and the fear all point to B.

questions.story: Flush A is the second red day, mid-range, with the VIX at 14 and the index at highs. Flush B is the fourth red day, into the prior breakout level, with the VIX at 31 and breadth washed out.

questions.q: Forced selling in a good business grades better than a business-changing collapse.
questions.why: True. Forced selling or an overreaction, not a broken business, is an A+ cue. A real change in the business makes the dead-cat bounce the likely path.
questions.lesson_line: Overreaction is a setup. A broken business is not.

questions.q: Take the turn?
choices: Pass; the business changed
Take it; 20% is a washout
Take it with a tight stop
questions.why: Pass. When the news is a real change in the business, the dead-cat bounce is the likely path. Bulkowski: once the bounce completes, price resumes declining.
questions.lesson_line: A broken business bounces, then keeps falling.

wrong.Take it; 20% is a washout: The size of the drop is not the issue. A real change in the business is.
wrong.Take it with a tight stop: A tight stop cannot fix a broken story. The bounce is the likely path to fail.

questions.story: A leader drops 20% in a day after a guidance cut and a fraud probe. It bounces intraday and the chart looks stretched.

questions.q: Linda Raschke will not trade against a market whose ADX is above 32 and rising.
questions.why: True. That is her filter against fading a strong trend. She also wants to see it fail twice at a level first.
questions.lesson_line: Do not fade a strong trend. Wait for it to fail.

questions.q: Stockbee says a trend has to exist before mean reversion can kick in.
questions.why: True. Bonde: a trend has to exist before mean reversion can kick in. StockCharts, on Connors, agrees: buy dips above the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Mean reversion rides on a trend, not against none.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Get out
Use 36.80 as the new stop
Hold for the bounce
questions.why: Get out. If the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out. Under 2R, the first 30-minute low becomes the new stop.
questions.lesson_line: Past 2R on the gap, get out.

wrong.Use 36.80 as the new stop: That works only under 2R. At 36.80 the loss is past 2R, so get out.
wrong.Hold for the bounce: The stop only moves up, and the gap ceiling is 2R. Get out.

questions.story: You bought at 40.00 with the stop at 38.50. The stock gaps down and the first 30 minutes make a low of 36.80, still falling.

questions.q: Take it?
choices: Take it; market order, stop under low
Wait for the close of the next day
Pass; the report is too close
questions.answer: Take it; market order, stop under low
questions.why: Take it. A leader above both averages, up 30%, four down days, a level, the turn printed, a report five days out. Market order, stop a few cents under the flush low.
questions.lesson_line: All gates pass: buy the turn at market, stop under the low.

wrong.Wait for the close of the next day: The turn is the trigger. Waiting for another close buys later and at a worse price.
wrong.Pass; the report is too close: The rule is no new buys in the 3 days before a report. Five days out is clear.

questions.story: A leader is up 30% over three months, above its 50-day and 200-day. It falls four days to its rising 50-day, then trades back over the prior day's low. Its report is five days away.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the flush day just closed. Wait for the turn, or pass?
choices: Wait for the turn; far above the 200-day
Pass; it is under the 200-day
Buy this close; the drop is huge
questions.answer: Wait for the turn; far above the 200-day
questions.why: Wait for the turn. An earnings flush, 13% under the rising 50-day in a stock still 20% above its 200-day. The next day it turned and closed at 3R.
questions.lesson_line: A leader flush well above the 200-day: wait for the turn.

wrong.Pass; it is under the 200-day: Look again: price sits well above a rising 200-day.
wrong.Buy this close; the drop is huge: Buying the close of the flush is a B-minus. We wait for the turn.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the flush day just closed. Take the turn, or pass?
choices: Pass; it closed under the 200-day
Take the turn; leaders always bounce
Take the turn; the drop is deep
questions.why: Pass. The flush closed 3.0% under the 200-day, and it is not a parabolic long: no burst, no 40% fall. B26 says watch only.
questions.lesson_line: A flush under the 200-day is watch only.

wrong.Take the turn; leaders always bounce: Nothing always bounces, and a close under the 200-day is a no-long unless the burst is there.
wrong.Take the turn; the drop is deep: The drop is a few days, not a burst. No longs below the 200-day unless it is a parabolic long.

conflicts: Provisional unit id: the unit plan (docs/study/UNITS-method.md) has no row for Mean Reversion, so this unit is written from the criteria card alone. SET.51, the skill id setup.mean_reversion and the file name are provisional pending D-002 (the setup map). Teaches, rungs and drills are the author's.

Pending-owner criteria kept OUT of every key and wrong note (the course's current default, waiting on the owner): mr.definition and the hold length of 1 to 5 sessions (D-016; q01 keys the idea only); mr.forms (D-002; no question quizzes the forms as a rule); mr.leader_rs, an RS rating for form A (D-011; no question; C31's exemption is not keyed); mr.prior_trend_b, the index exception below the 200-day (D-009; the stock questions key B26 as written, no index or ETF question); mr.stretch_count, how many of the five marks are needed (D-114; no question names a count and the which-is-not-a-mark question lists marks only; the META 2024-07-15 near-miss, which fails on that count, is not used); mr.volume, 1.5x the 50-day (D-006; no key; the AMZN 2024-04-22 near-miss is not used); mr.trigger, which turn counts (D-003; the buy-the-turn questions key only 'the turn, not the falling price' and that buying the close of the flush is B-minus on the card, the one thing every option but (c) shares); mr.stop_width, 3% and size down or skip (D-005; the stop-width question keys only 'never pull the stop in'; the DASH story is keyed on 'no level to lean on'); mr.trims, Option 2 first trim at the 20-day (D-013; the Kell question gives Kell's target as Kell's and keys the house thirds); mr.time_stop, 3 sessions (D-019; the time-stop question keys C33's 10 days only); mr.short_above_200 and the short mirror (D-009, D-001; no short question); mr.market_reading, Orange and Red markets (D-023; no market-reading question).

The five stretch marks (mr.mark_atr_drop, mr.mark_band, mr.mark_rsi2, mr.mark_down_days, mr.mark_blowoff) are proposed on the card, not owner rulings; every question keyed on one carries house: true and cites the card's own statement. The dossier's scan found the count of marks describes the stretch but does not predict the bounce, so no question treats more marks as a better bounce except through the card's own grade rows (the 4th down day or later).

Bollinger says closes outside the bands are at first continuation signals (bl2 is cited in no key); the card makes a close under the lower band a stretch mark, never the trigger. The band questions key the card's wording: a tag is not a mark, a close under is.

Stops: Connors uses none and Alvarez found max-loss stops did not help his tests (but 'I am not saying one should trade mean reversion without stops'); Kell, Kullamagi and Bracco use a tight stop at the day's extreme. A3 and D41 win; the no-stop questions teach Connors' plan as a plan we do not use.

Entry: Connors buys the close, Alvarez found a limit order below the close did better, Kullamagi and Breitstein wait for the turn. The card waits for the turn (D-003 is open on which turn); our entries are market orders (E57).

ELF 2024-04-04 is filed under two criteria: the card's failure list says mr.prior_trend_a (a broken leader after a parabolic top) and dossier section 14 says mr.inv_stall (the turn day closed in the bottom 3% of its range). The ELF question asks the broken-leader reading, which the dossier's own lesson sentence states; the stall is taught in the early-warning question and the SBUX story.

The lookalike tells (tMA, tPa1, tPa2, tUR, tOo) are the card's own statements about the neighbouring cards; the parabolic long's thresholds (3 to 5 down days, two gaps, a 40% fall or a 5 ATR stretch) belong to that card and may still be pending there. The parabolic-long question is keyed on the type (a multi-day burst of gap downs), not on a threshold.

Examples (d1) are read off our own daily bars by the research scan (dossier sections 13 and 14), not from a public page or an owner ruling; the scan covers today's tickers only (survivorship) and five of its ten extremes were earnings reactions. The owner has not yet reviewed the ten names. Walk-through and story numbers depend on it. The base rate (29.8% to 3R, 76% stopped within 20 sessions on a fixed stop) is a research proxy and is not used in any key.

Walk-through fills: the scan bought at the open if it gapped above the flush close, otherwise at the flush close plus a cent, and put the stop 5 cents under the lower of the flush low and the turn day's low (A13, F62); a live market order fills a little differently.

The chart questions (KRYS asof 2023-08-07, the flush day itself; LLY asof 2025-03-10, taken as the trading day before the 2025-03-11 turn day, the flush day) show the member's own chart with their averages; the ticker is not in the question. The keys rest on dossier reads (dKR1, dKR2, dLL1, dLL2). If the importer's bars start the forward window one day off, the reveal text still holds.
The stock questions apply B26 (no longs below the 200-day, unless a parabolic long) as written; the card's index exception is D-009 and is not taught here.

The Kell question teaches Kell's retest of the 20 EMA as Kell's own target; the dossier recommends a similar first trim for this setup (Option 2, pending D-013). If the owner adopts Option 2, the 3R fill, 3R price, trim-at-open and breakeven questions need a second look.

The time-stop question keys C33's 10 trading days as the general time stop. The card's own time stop for this setup (3 sessions without a close above the flush day's high) is pending D-019 and may replace it.
